exposure: Mode of delivery (Caesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
outcome: Maternal infection (endometritis, caesarean or perineal wound infection, or urinary tract infection)
Newborn infection (umbilical cord infection or possible severe bacterial infection)
cohort: 791 women and their newborns following hospital childbirth in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania
finding: Telephone surveillance identified a substantial risk of postnatal infection, with Caesarean section being the most significant risk factor for maternal infection, highlighting the urgent need for improved pre-operative antibiotic prophylaxis in this setting.
mod_finding: Caesarean childbirth was associated with a higher risk of maternal infection compared to vaginal delivery.
